To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
short time fasting will increase the lithogenicity of the bile and that this increase is not related to a rise in the cholesterol saturation index.
weight reduction by fasting for 4 weeks in patients with obesity and non-alcoholic steatohepatitis is not sufficient for a normalization of the metabolic and hepatic situation.

a 4-week weight reduction of 7.5 +/- 3.5% (p < 0.01) in 13 patients with morbid obesity and a mean CSI of 1.35 was accompanied by a significant reduction of the mean biliary cholesterol saturation index from 1.36 +/- 0.34 to 1.18 +/- 0.63 (p < 1.0).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question, if weight reduction is a sufficient therapy to prevent the development of gallstone disease in patients with morbid obesity.
the question whether weight reduction can be a risk factor to develop gallstones.
the question of whether a 4-week fasting period (452 kCal/day) is sufficient to prevent gallstone formation in obese patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a 4 weeks' fasting period is not sufficient to reduce biliary lithogenic factors to normal values.
a short time weight reduction is not recommended for obese patients with gallstones.
weight reduction is a necessary precondition for the prevention of gallstone formation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a short fasting period of 4 weeks with 452 kcal/day will be a risk for the development of cholesterol gallstones, if no weight and metabolic normalisations can be achieved.

a weight reduction by 5% of body weight within 4 weeks is sufficient to improve the biliary lithogenic potential, if the weight reduction is accompanied by an improved glycoprotein metabolism and an improvement of gallbladder contractibility.
the lithogenicity is increased after short time fasting in patients with normal CSI.
The main takeaway from our work is that
short-term fasting is a risk factor for cholesterol gallstone formation.
short time fasting is a risk factor for developing gallstones, and it is important that weight normalization and metabolic improvement are achieved.
weight loss is a very important aspect of the management of obesity.
